desc:
A referee writes down scores on a sheet, one entry after another, and sometimes corrects the sheet. You are given the list ops; each element is one action:

  • A value x ≥ 0: a new score x is written at the end of the sheet.
  • -1: the last score still on the sheet is crossed out and no longer counts.
  • -2: a new score equal to twice the last score still on the sheet is written.
  • -3: a new score equal to the sum of the last two scores still on the sheet is written.

Return the sum of all scores that remain on the sheet after every action. The actions are always possible: whenever one refers to the last one or two scores, they exist.

Example: [5, 2, -1, -2, -3]: the sheet is [5, 2], then [5], then [5, 10], then [5, 10, 15], so the answer is 30.
constraints: Every element is either -1, -2, -3 or a score between 0 and 100,000
Every score written by a -2 or -3 action is at most 100,000
Each action has the scores it needs on the sheet
hints: Only the end of the sheet is ever read or changed.
Keep the scores that are still valid in a list where you only append and remove at the end.
Use a stack. A score pushes its value, -1 pops, -2 pushes 2 * top, -3 pushes top + second from top. Return the sum of the stack at the end.
editorial: The sheet behaves as a stack: every action reads or removes the newest scores and every new score goes on top. Walk through ops once, maintain the list of valid scores, and apply each action to its end.

For the sum of the last two scores, read stack[-1] + stack[-2] before pushing. A cancelled score is simply popped, so later actions see the entry below it. At the end return sum(stack). Every action takes O(1), so the total is O(n) time and O(n) space. With at most 5,000 actions and scores at most 100,000 the total stays below 231.
